system_description.narrative_title: China's economic-political pivot reshaping global markets and industries
system_description.narrative_summary: Across the headlines a single dominant narrative emerges: China's domestic political tightening, export controls and geopolitical posture are interacting with slowing domestic demand to reshape global industries and trigger market volatility. Corporate earnings misses and AI-related uncertainty amplify investor reactions in tech, chips and autos, while regulatory moves at home and abroad (sanctions, bans, export curbs) produce strategic shifts by multinationals. The situation behaves as an open system with policy, markets, corporate strategy and geopolitical events in continuous feedback.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: Chinese domestic politics and economic policy (party discipline, export controls, official statistics), China's industrial sectors (tech, semiconductors, autos, payments), multinational corporate performance and strategy tied to China (earnings, write-downs, market access), global capital markets and investor sentiment, regulatory and sanctioning actions by other states, and regional incidents (Taiwan waters, Hong Kong fire, public backlash).
system_description.super_system: The integrated global political‑economy of trade, supply chains and capital markets
adjacent_subsystems: Global capital markets and investor sentiment
Semiconductor supply chain and AI hardware ecosystem
Global automotive value chain (EVs and China‑developed tech)
Regional security and diplomacy (Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan, EU relations)

variables.name: Political control level
variables.description: Degree of centralized political tightening and internal discipline within governing structures, measured as the intensity and scope of top-down political directives and internal purges.

variables.name: Policy enforcement intensity
variables.description: Rate and vigor with which new and existing policies (regulatory, export or security) are implemented and enforced across economic and administrative channels.

variables.name: Export restriction level
variables.description: Stringency and breadth of controls limiting cross-border transfer of goods, technologies and services, including licensing, blacklists and practical barriers.

variables.name: Advanced technology accessibility
variables.description: Degree to which advanced technologies (designs, equipment, know‑how) are available to domestic and foreign firms through trade, licensing and supply arrangements.

variables.name: Domestic demand growth rate
variables.description: Rate of change in internal consumer and business demand for goods and services within the domestic economy.

variables.name: Industrial capacity utilization
variables.description: Proportion of productive industrial capacity currently in use relative to potential maximum output across key manufacturing sectors.

variables.name: Global supply chain resilience
variables.description: System-wide ability of international supply networks to absorb disruptions, re-route inputs and maintain delivery of critical components.

variables.name: Multinational market accessibility
variables.description: Ease with which foreign-affiliated firms can enter, operate and sell in the domestic market, including licensing, joint-venture barriers and informal constraints.

variables.name: Corporate earnings surprise rate
variables.description: Frequency and magnitude of firms' reported earnings deviating from market expectations over time.

variables.name: Investor sentiment
variables.description: Aggregate market perception of risk and return prospects for assets exposed to the system, reflecting confidence, fear and forward-looking expectations.

variables.name: Capital market volatility level
variables.description: Degree of price variability and risk premia in equity, bond and currency markets influenced by system shocks and uncertainty.

variables.name: Cross-border investment flows
variables.description: Net and gross movements of capital across borders for direct investment, portfolio allocation and M&A activity.

variables.name: Regulatory policy activity rate
variables.description: Pace at which new rules, guidance and formal regulatory changes are issued by authorities and relevant regulators.

variables.name: Geopolitical incident frequency
variables.description: Rate at which regional political or security incidents occur that affect cross-border trade, navigation or diplomatic relations.

variables.name: Public backlash intensity
variables.description: Level of social, consumer and media-driven backlash against firms, cultural products or foreign actors, measured by protests, boycotts and social-media amplification.

variables.name: Corporate strategy reorientation rate
variables.description: Speed at which firms alter supply chains, investment plans, product strategies and market allocations in response to evolving policy and market signals.

catalysts.title: CCP disciplinary purge and loyalty drive
catalysts.description: Sustained internal purges and loyalty campaigns within the Communist Party tighten political control and accelerate policy enforcement across agencies.
catalysts.rationale: China’s Communist Party confirms expulsions; Xi Demands More Loyalty as Purges Trim Party Elite; conclave on toughening discipline

catalysts.title: Expansion of export curbs on AI technologies
catalysts.description: China broadens export controls around advanced AI components and 'crown-jewel' technologies, restricting outbound transfers and licensing.
catalysts.rationale: China's new export curbs draw a line around its AI crown jewels

catalysts.title: US/allied tech and import bans broaden
catalysts.description: US and allied measures extend bans on Chinese labs, telecom access and select exporters, further constraining tech links and trade.
catalysts.rationale: US bans imports from BGI/MGI; FCC votes to ban Chinese labs; US plans ban on Chinese telecom firms

catalysts.title: Increased PLA naval activity near Taiwan
catalysts.description: Sustained Chinese naval sweeps and data collection near Taiwan raise regional tensions and incident risk, affecting trade and investor confidence.
catalysts.rationale: Taiwan flags 'obvious' threat from 50 Chinese vessels; China scoops up data that could aid its forces

catalysts.title: Global auto industry reshuffle driven by China
catalysts.description: Weak domestic auto demand and strong export push prompt firms to globalise China-developed tech and reorient strategies and capacity.
catalysts.rationale: China’s Car Industry crashing at home; BYD’s export surge; Volkswagen plans to globalise China-developed technology

catalysts.title: Broader rollout of foreign payment services in China
catalysts.description: Following regulatory green lights, foreign payment providers deepen partnerships and expand services, altering market access and flows.
catalysts.rationale: Tencent, Visa deepen payments push in China after regulatory green light

catalysts.title: Ongoing consumer-nationalism and brand backlash
catalysts.description: Episodes of social- and media-driven backlash against foreign brands persist, affecting sales, reputations and market access for targeted firms.
catalysts.rationale: Sanrio cuts ties after China backlash; Chinese brands target Mbappé and Hello Kitty; Real Madrid apologies

catalysts.title: Chip-sector rout and regulatory probes
catalysts.description: Sharp sell-offs and regulatory scrutiny in the semiconductor sector (Intel rout, exec probes) drive volatility and reassessment of tech exposure.
catalysts.rationale: Intel plunges triggering global chip rout; Chinese exec close to Nvidia CEO suspected in probe

catalysts.title: Hong Kong safety and regulatory reform process
catalysts.description: Post-fire inquiries and pledged reforms accelerate regulatory activity in Hong Kong, with implications for governance and market operations.
catalysts.rationale: Hong Kong leader apologises for deadly Tai Po fire, pledges reform; inquiries into 2025 fire
